mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over 60-day walk-forward window, no statistically significant negative returns (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold upward, compared to prior month’s return.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims exceeding 10,000 suggests weakening labor demand, which coincides with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investors anticipate earnings compression.
failure_condition: In regimes where unemployment is not structurally high, the signal does not produce a statistically significant negative return (p > 0.05) over the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in homebuilding activity (HOUST) of at least 5% for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as construction spending weakness signals broader economic softness.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous_month and HOUST < two_months_ago by >= 5%
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in non-crisis periods when HOUST declines are not structural.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 3% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating supply capacity, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as market anticipates profit margin compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous_month and INDPRO > two_months_ago and INDPRO > three_months_ago by >= 3%
failure_condition: No significant negative 20-day forward return (p > 0.05) when INDPRO growth is not followed by earnings disappointments.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains above 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as the market anticipates a protracted tightening cycle that eventually supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous_month and CPIAUCSL > two_months_ago by > 3%
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, the forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when inflation does not subsequently peak or recede as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) to above 5% triggers a negative S&P 60-day forward return as market anticipates a labor market slowdown and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: In non-recessionary regimes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses the 5% threshold without broader economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail sales (not directly available in the catalog, so this sketch is omitted) would be the logical next step for demand proxies. Instead, we use a demand interaction: when both RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (homebuilding) decline by at least 2% in the same month, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to dual demand weakness.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05) when both proxies decline but market sentiment remains stable (e.g., low volatility).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) of 4% or more for three consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates a supply-side normalization that supports pricing power.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < previous_month and RSAFS < two_months_ago and RSAFS < three_months_ago by >= 4%
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward return (p > 0.05) when RSAFS declines are not followed by a subsequent rebound in earnings or GDP growth.
